title: Robotic Arm Link - Combined Bending and Torsion
studentDocumentTitle: Student Packet - Robotic Arm Link - Combined Bending and Torsion
instructorDocumentTitle: Instructor Guide - Robotic Arm Link - Combined Bending and Torsion
summary: Evaluate bending, torsion, von Mises stress, and static-yield margin at the root of an equivalent hollow circular robot-arm link.
imageAttribution: Nenad Stojković (Shixart1985), Robot arm works on a small component in a lab setting, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0. Visual context only; no numerical value is inferred from the photograph.
idealizedImageAlt: Instructor reference equivalent hollow circular cantilever link under payload bending, self-weight bending, and applied torque.
problemStatement: Model the selected robot-arm link as a uniform hollow circular cantilever. Use payload mass mp = {{robot_link_mp_kg}} {{robot_link_mp_kg_unit}}, length L = {{robot_link_L_mm}} {{robot_link_L_mm_unit}}, link mass mL = {{robot_link_mL_kg}} {{robot_link_mL_kg_unit}}, wall thickness t = {{robot_link_t_mm}} {{robot_link_t_mm_unit}}, equivalent outer diameter Do = {{robot_link_Do_mm}} {{robot_link_Do_mm_unit}}, torque T = {{robot_link_T_Nm}} {{robot_link_T_Nm_unit}}, and yield strength Sy = {{robot_link_Sy_MPa}} {{robot_link_Sy_MPa_unit}}. Use fixed g = 9.81 m/s2.
engineeringGoal: Determine the fixed-root bending and torsional stresses, von Mises equivalent stress, and static-yield factor of safety; identify the dominant contribution and make a bounded mechanics-based recommendation.
